seeds.goal: You can fill in a simple form about yourself: name, age, city, school, hobby, and one sentence about what you like.
seeds.why: Every language school, hostel, competition and online course starts with a form. If you can fill it in without help, nobody has to translate for you.
seeds.ex: Aigerim filled in a form for a free online course. Eight lines, no mistakes — and she was accepted the same evening.
seeds.read: Read the form and find one thing: what does Aigerim want to do in the future?
seeds.task: Fill in a form about yourself (30–50 words): your name, age, city, school, one hobby and one sentence about your plans.
model: I live in Almaty, in Kazakhstan.
I live with my mother, my father and my little brother.
Say what you want to do
I want to be a designer.
sent: I live in Almaty with my family.
My father works in a bank.
I have two brothers and one sister.
I can speak Kazakh, Russian and English.
I want to be a designer.
topics: My name is Aigerim and I am fifteen. I live in Almaty and I study at school number 25.
This form is about me.
I draw every evening. I also like taking photos of my city.
My free time is all about pictures.
I speak Kazakh at home, Russian at school and English in my online course.
I use three languages every day.
ideas: The colour of my phone case
seeds.title: About me: a form
seeds.sub: Name, age, city, hobbies — the first form you fill in

seeds.goal: You can write a short message that says where you are, what happened and when you will arrive.
seeds.why: Your friend is waiting at the cinema and your bus is stuck. Two English sentences save the evening — and they are the same two sentences you will need abroad.
seeds.ex: Marat wrote four lines to his host brother in London: where he was, why he was late, when he would come. Nobody worried.
seeds.read: Read the message and find one thing: what time will Marat arrive?
seeds.task: Write a message to your friend (25–45 words): say where you are, what the problem is, when you will come and say sorry.
model: I am at the bus stop near the school.
My bus is late because of the snow.
I will be at the cinema at seven.
sent: I am at the bus stop near the school.
My bus is late because of the snow.
I will be at the cinema at seven.
I am really sorry about this.
The film starts at half past seven.
I do not have my phone charger.
My mother drives me to the centre.
I waited twenty minutes in the cold.
We can meet in front of the cinema.
topics: My bus did not come. I waited twenty minutes in the snow.
I have a small problem this evening.
The film starts at half past seven. I will be there at seven.
We still have enough time.
Can you buy two tickets? I will give you the money tomorrow.
I need one favour from you.
ideas: A long story about my week
seeds.title: A message to a friend
seeds.sub: Where you are and when you will come

seeds.goal: You can write a postcard: where you are, what the weather is like, what you do every day and one thing you love.
seeds.why: A postcard is the shortest travel story in the world. Four sentences, and the person at home can see the place.
seeds.ex: Aizhan sent a postcard from Antalya: 38 words, no mistakes. Her teacher put it on the classroom wall.
seeds.read: Read the postcard and find one thing: what does Aizhan like most about this holiday?
seeds.task: Write a postcard from your holiday (30–50 words): where you are, the weather, what you do every day, one thing you love, and a warm goodbye.
model: We are in a small hotel near the sea.
Say what the weather is like
The weather here is hot and sunny every day.
Say what you do every day
We swim in the morning and walk in the old town in the evening.
I love the smell of the sea.
sent: We are in a small hotel near the sea.
The weather here is hot and sunny.
We swim in the morning every day.
The beach is five minutes from our room.
I bought a small souvenir for my sister.
The food in the market is very cheap.
My brother does not like the hot sun.
We walk in the old town after dinner.
I can see the sea from my window.
topics: We swim before breakfast and walk in the old town after dinner. Every day is the same and I love it.
Our days here have a simple shape.
The sun is hot from ten in the morning until six in the evening. There was no rain this week.
The weather is the best part of this holiday.
I bought a small souvenir for my sister and a magnet for my mother.
I am bringing home some small presents.
ideas: The price of my plane ticket
A problem with my phone battery
seeds.title: A postcard
seeds.sub: Four warm lines from your holiday

seeds.goal: You can write one or two sentences under a photo: who is in it, where it is and why the moment matters.
seeds.why: Captions are the shortest writing in the world and the most read. One good line under a photo teaches you word order faster than a page of grammar.
seeds.ex: Nurlan wrote captions for his school photo exhibition. Twelve photos, twelve sentences — and every visitor understood the story.
seeds.read: Read the captions and find one thing: which photo was taken in the morning?
seeds.task: Write four captions for four photos (20–40 words in total): who is in the photo, where, when, and one detail that makes the moment special.
model: Say who is in the photo
This is my grandmother in her garden.
Say where the photo was taken
The photo was taken in our village near Taraz.
It was early in the morning, before the heat.
She is picking apples for the winter.
Her old blue scarf is in every family photo.
I like this picture because she is laughing.
phr: In this photo you can see …
Мне нравится это фото, потому что …
sent: This is my grandmother in her garden.
The photo was taken in our village.
She is picking apples for the winter.
It was early in the morning.
My little cousin is smiling at the camera.
The old blue scarf is in every family photo.
We visit this village every summer.
I like this picture because she is laughing.
My father took this photo with his phone.
There are three generations in one picture.
topics: She is picking apples and laughing. The basket is already full.
This photo shows my grandmother at work.
It was six in the morning and the air was still cool. The sun is very low in the picture.
The light tells you the time of day.
My father, my grandmother and my cousin are in the same frame.
Three generations in one photo.
ideas: How many photos I have on my phone
seeds.title: A photo caption
seeds.sub: One sentence that explains the picture

seeds.goal: You can write a clear to-do list with days, times and short notes that another person can understand.
seeds.why: A list is the first English text you will write for someone else: a note on the fridge, a task list for a group project, a plan for your week abroad.
seeds.ex: Dias made an English to-do list for his exchange week. His host family read it and helped him with two tasks he could not do alone.
seeds.read: Read the list and find one thing: what does Dias have to do before Friday?
seeds.task: Write a to-do list for your week (30–50 words): four or five tasks with days and times, and one short note for the person who reads it.
model: Write the first task with a day
Monday: buy a notebook and a pen.
Write a task with a time
Wednesday at 5 p.m.: English lesson online.
Write a task for another person
Thursday: help my brother with his maths.
Friday: finish the school project before 6 p.m.
Saturday: football with my friends in the park.
Add one note for the reader
Note: I need money for the bus on Wednesday.
phr: That is all for this week.
sent: On Monday I buy a notebook and a pen.
My English lesson is at five o'clock.
I have to finish the project before Friday.
I help my brother with his maths.
We play football in the park on Saturday.
I do not have money for the bus.
My mother works late on Wednesday.
The library closes at six in the evening.
I can do two tasks in one evening.
Do not forget my school bag.
topics: Buy a notebook on Monday. Finish the project on Friday. Play football on Saturday.
This is my plan for the week.
My English lesson is at five and my brother needs help at six.
Wednesday is my busiest day.
I need money for the bus and a new pen for school.
There are two things I have to buy.
ideas: What exactly I have to do
What I think about school food
seeds.title: A to-do list with notes
seeds.sub: Plans for the week in short lines

seeds.goal: You can invite a person: give the day, the time, the place, one detail about the event and ask for an answer.
seeds.why: An invitation that forgets the time or the address is not an invitation. This is the first text where a missing detail has real consequences.
seeds.ex: Kamila invited eight classmates in English. Everyone came at the right time — because every message had the same four facts.
seeds.read: Read the invitation and find one thing: what does Kamila ask her friends to bring?
seeds.task: Write an invitation to your birthday party (30–50 words): the day, the time, the place, what you will do, what to bring, and ask your friend to answer.
model: Say what you invite them to
I am having a birthday party on Saturday.
Give the day and the time
It starts at six o'clock in the evening.
We are at my flat, Abay Street 14, flat 9.
We will eat pizza, listen to music and play games.
Can you tell me before Friday?
phr: I am having a party on …
I would like to invite you.
sent: I am having a birthday party on Saturday.
It starts at six o'clock in the evening.
We are at my flat on Abay Street.
We will eat pizza and listen to music.
My mother makes a big cake every year.
Ten friends are coming to the party.
Can you tell me before Friday?
The party finishes at ten o'clock.
I do not need a present.
topics: It starts at six on Saturday at my flat on Abay Street.
Here are the details of the party.
We will eat pizza, listen to music and play two games.
This is what we are going to do.
Bring your favourite song and tell me before Friday.
There are two things I need from you.
ideas: The story of my last birthday
seeds.title: An invitation
seeds.sub: Come to my party: when, where, what to bring

seeds.goal: You can describe your family: how many people, who they are, what they do and one detail about each.
seeds.why: This is the text every host family, teacher and new classmate asks for first. Get it right once and you can say it for years.
seeds.ex: Dias wrote six sentences about his family for an exchange programme. The host family printed it and put it on the fridge.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: who is the youngest person in this family?
seeds.task: Write about your family (30–50 words): how many people, who they are, what they do, and one detail that makes each person special.
model: Say how many people there are
There are five people in my family.
My mother is a nurse and my father drives a taxi.
Say who else lives with you
I have a big brother and a little sister.
My sister is only four years old and she talks all day.
Say where the older family lives
My grandparents live in a village near Shymkent.
We have dinner together every evening.
I love my family very much.
phr: There are … people in my family.
sent: There are five people in my family.
My mother is a nurse in a hospital.
My father drives a taxi in the city.
I have a big brother and a little sister.
My sister is only four years old.
My grandparents live in a village.
We have dinner together every evening.
My brother studies at the university.
I do not have any cousins in Almaty.
We visit our grandmother every summer.
topics: My mother is a nurse and my father drives a taxi. My brother studies at the university.
Everybody in my family works or studies.
We have dinner together every evening and watch a film on Sunday.
We spend our evenings together.
My grandparents live in a village and we visit them every summer.
Part of my family lives far from the city.
ideas: A film about a family I watched
seeds.title: My family
seeds.sub: Who they are and what they do

seeds.goal: You can describe a room: what is in it, where things are and what you do there.
seeds.why: Describing a place teaches you the two things English uses constantly: there is / there are and prepositions of place.
seeds.ex: Aruzhan described her room in eight sentences for a school website. Her teacher used it as the model text for the whole class.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what can Aruzhan see from her window?
seeds.task: Describe your room (30–50 words): its size, three things in it, where they are, and what you usually do there.
model: Say how big the room is
My room is small but very light.
Name the main things in it
There is a bed, a desk and a big bookcase.
The desk is next to the window.
From my window I can see the mountains.
My favourite thing is an old lamp from my grandmother.
I do my homework and listen to music in this room.
It is the quietest place in our flat.
phr: From my window I can see …
Мне нравится моя комната, потому что …
sent: My room is small but very light.
There is a bed and a big bookcase.
The desk is next to the window.
From my window I can see the mountains.
My favourite thing is an old lamp.
I do my homework in this room.
The walls in my room are white.
My brother does not come in without knocking.
I put my photos on the wall last year.
There are two carpets on the floor.
topics: There is a bed, a desk and a bookcase. The desk stands next to the window.
My room has everything I need.
I do my homework here and listen to music in the evening.
This room is where I work and rest.
The lamp on my desk was my grandmother's. It is fifty years old.
One old thing in my room has a story.
ideas: Three things and where they are
What I do in the room
The price of my new phone
What my friend's room looks like
seeds.title: My room
seeds.sub: A place a reader can picture

seeds.goal: You can describe your normal day with times, from morning to evening, and say what is different at the weekend.
seeds.why: This text trains the present simple and time prepositions — the two things that break first when you speak English under pressure.
seeds.ex: Nurislam wrote his day for a summer camp application. The camp used it to put him in the right group.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what does Nurislam do differently on Sunday?
seeds.task: Describe your normal day (35–55 words): what you do in the morning, at school, after school and in the evening, with times — and one thing that is different at the weekend.
model: I get up at half past six every morning.
I have breakfast with my family at seven.
My lessons start at eight and finish at two.
Say what you do after school
After school I play basketball for an hour.
Say what you do in the evening
In the evening I do my homework and read.
Say when you go to bed
I go to bed at about eleven o'clock.
Say what is different at the weekend
On Sunday I sleep until ten and visit my grandmother.
sent: I get up at half past six every morning.
I have breakfast with my family at seven.
My lessons start at eight and finish at two.
After school I play basketball for an hour.
In the evening I do my homework.
I go to bed at about eleven o'clock.
On Sunday I sleep until ten.
My mother wakes up before everybody else.
I do not watch television on school days.
I visited my grandmother last Sunday.
topics: I get up at half past six, have breakfast at seven and leave home at half past seven.
My mornings are always the same.
I play basketball after school and do my homework after dinner.
My afternoons have two parts.
On Sunday I sleep until ten and visit my grandmother.
The weekend has its own timetable.
ideas: What is different at the weekend
What I do in the evening
seeds.title: My day
seeds.sub: Times, actions and one exception

seeds.goal: You can describe an animal: what it looks like, what it does, what it eats and why you like it.
seeds.why: A pet text is the easiest way to learn adjectives and the present simple with he, she and it — and everyone wants to read it.
seeds.ex: Alua wrote about her cat for an online pen-friend. The reply came back with four questions — the text worked.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what does the cat do every morning?
seeds.task: Write about your pet, or an animal you would like (30–50 words): its name, what it looks like, what it does every day, what it eats and why you like it.
model: I have a cat and her name is Mia.
She is grey with one white ear.
Say what it does every day
Every morning she wakes me up at six.
She eats fish and drinks a lot of water.
She is very quiet but she does not like guests.
I like Mia because she waits for me after school.
phr: She is part of the family.
sent: I have a cat and her name is Mia.
She is grey with one white ear.
Every morning she wakes me up at six.
She eats fish and drinks a lot of water.
My cat does not like loud music.
We found her in the street two years ago.
She sleeps on my bed every night.
I take my dog for a walk after school.
She can open the kitchen door.
topics: She is grey with one white ear and green eyes.
My cat is easy to recognise.
She wakes me up at six and waits for me after school.
Mia knows my timetable better than I do.
We found her in the street two years ago and she stayed.
Mia came to us by accident.
seeds.title: My pet
seeds.sub: An animal the reader can see

seeds.goal: You can describe a dish: what is in it, when you eat it, who makes it and why you like it.
seeds.why: Food is the first topic in every conversation abroad. Writing about it first makes speaking about it automatic.
seeds.ex: Timur wrote about beshbarmak for an international school blog. Three readers asked for the recipe.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: when does Timur's family eat this dish?
seeds.task: Write about your favourite food (30–50 words): what it is, what is in it, when you eat it, who makes it and why you love it.
model: It is meat, thin pasta and onion.
My grandmother makes it better than anybody.
We eat it when the whole family comes together.
It is warm, salty and very simple.
I remember the smell in my grandmother's kitchen.
I love this food because it means family for me.
sent: It is meat, thin pasta and onion.
My grandmother makes it better than anybody.
We eat it when the family comes together.
It tastes warm and a little salty.
I do not like very spicy food.
My mother cooked plov last Sunday.
We buy the meat in the small market.
You should try it with hot bread.
topics: It is meat, thin pasta and onion, and nothing else.
The dish is simpler than people think.
We eat it when the whole family comes together, four or five times a year.
This food belongs to special days.
I remember the smell in my grandmother's kitchen every time I eat it.
For me this dish is a memory.
ideas: The price of meat in the market
A restaurant I did not like
seeds.title: My favourite food
seeds.sub: A dish, a taste and a moment

seeds.goal: You can write your timetable in sentences: which subjects, on which days, at what times, and which one you like most.
seeds.why: Turning a table into sentences is a real skill: it teaches days, times and the difference between have and there is.
seeds.ex: Aliya sent her timetable to an online tutor. The tutor found two free evenings and planned the lessons around them.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: which day is the longest for Aliya?
seeds.task: Write about your timetable (35–55 words): how many lessons you have, which subjects on which days, your longest day, and the subject you like most and why.
model: Say how many lessons you have
I have six lessons every day.
The school day starts at eight o'clock.
On Monday I have maths, English, history and biology.
Say which day is the longest
Thursday is my longest day because I have seven lessons.
I like it because we talk a lot in the lesson.
On Friday I finish early, at one o'clock.
phr: That is my week at school.
sent: I have six lessons every day.
The school day starts at eight o'clock.
On Monday I have maths and English.
We have a long break at eleven.
Our history teacher gives a lot of homework.
I do not have lessons on Sunday.
I can stay after school for the football club.
topics: On Monday I have maths, English, history and biology. Tuesday is almost the same.
The start of my week is full.
Thursday has seven lessons and Friday has only four.
My days are not the same length.
I like English because we talk in the lesson and nobody laughs at mistakes.
One subject is easy to enjoy.
ideas: The colour of the school building
What I ate in the canteen
seeds.title: My school timetable
seeds.sub: Days, subjects and one opinion

seeds.goal: You can describe the weather today and yesterday, and say what people wear because of it.
seeds.why: Weather is the safest small talk in English and the fastest way to practise it is / it was.
seeds.ex: Sanzhar wrote a daily weather line in English for a month. By the end he stopped translating in his head.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: what does Sanzhar advise his friend to wear?
seeds.task: Write a weather note for a friend who is coming to your city (25–45 words): the weather today, yesterday, the temperature, and what to wear.
model: Say what the weather is like today
It is cold and windy in Almaty today.
The temperature is about minus five.
Say what it was like yesterday
Yesterday it was warmer and there was no wind.
Say if it rains or snows
It snowed all night and the streets are white.
Bring a warm hat and thick shoes.
Tomorrow will be sunny but still cold.
sent: It is cold and windy in Almaty today.
The temperature is about minus five.
Yesterday it was warmer than today.
Bring a warm hat and thick shoes.
Tomorrow will be sunny but still cold.
I do not like rain in November.
The streets are white this morning.
Children play in the snow after school.
We had a very hot summer last year.
topics: It snowed all night and the temperature is minus five.
Today is a proper winter day.
Yesterday there was no wind and it was warmer. Today is different.
The weather changed overnight.
Bring a warm hat, thick shoes and gloves.
Here is what you need to pack.
ideas: A holiday I had in Turkey
seeds.title: A weather note
seeds.sub: What it is like outside, in four lines

seeds.goal: You can write a shopping list with quantities and a short note that tells another person where to go and what to do.
seeds.why: Quantities are where A1 English breaks: two breads, three milks. A list makes you fix that once and for all.
seeds.ex: Aizhan left an English shopping note for her host mother. Everything on the list came home correctly.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: which shop does Aizhan ask her brother to visit?
seeds.task: Write a shopping list and a short note (30–50 words): five things with quantities, which shop, how much money, and one thing not to forget.
model: Can you buy some things for dinner?
We need two loaves of bread, a litre of milk and six eggs.
We also need rice and a kilo of apples.
The small shop near the bus stop is cheaper.
The money is on the kitchen table.
sent: Can you buy some things for dinner?
We need two loaves of bread.
A litre of milk costs four hundred tenge.
We also need rice and six eggs.
The small shop near the bus stop is cheaper.
The money is on the kitchen table.
My mother goes to the market on Saturday.
We do not need sugar this week.
topics: Two loaves of bread, a litre of milk, six eggs, rice and a kilo of apples.
This is everything we need for dinner.
The small shop near the bus stop is cheaper than the supermarket.
Where you buy it matters.
The money is on the kitchen table and the bag is behind the door.
Everything is ready for you at home.
seeds.title: A shopping list and note
seeds.sub: What to buy and where

seeds.goal: You can describe a person: how you met, what they look like, what they are like and one thing you do together.
seeds.why: Describing people is the hardest A1 skill: it needs adjectives, present simple and one small story — all in five lines.
seeds.ex: Madina wrote about her best friend for a pen-friend project. Her partner in Poland wrote back the same day.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: where did Madina meet her best friend?
seeds.task: Write about your best friend (35–55 words): their name and age, how you met, what they look like, what they are like, and one thing you do together.
model: My best friend is called Dana and she is fifteen.
We met in the first class of primary school.
She is tall and she has short dark hair.
She is funny and she never talks behind your back.
Say what they are good at
She is very good at maths and she helps me with it.
Every Saturday we go to the swimming pool together.
I trust her more than anyone at school.
sent: My best friend is called Dana.
We met in the first class of primary school.
She is tall and has short dark hair.
She is funny and very kind.
She is good at maths and helps me.
Every Saturday we go to the swimming pool.
Dana does not like loud parties.
Last summer we worked in the same café.
I trust her more than anyone.
topics: She is tall, she has short dark hair and she always wears a red jacket.
Dana is easy to find in a crowd.
She is good at maths and she explains it better than the teacher.
Dana helps me where I am weakest.
Every Saturday we go to the swimming pool and eat ice cream after it.
We have one habit that never changes.
ideas: Name, age and how we met
What they are like as a person
A film we watched last year
My opinion about our school canteen
seeds.title: My best friend
seeds.sub: A person in five details

seeds.goal: You can describe your city or village: where it is, how big it is, what is interesting there and what you like about it.
seeds.why: Every conversation with a foreigner starts here. Five prepared sentences make you sound fluent for a whole minute.
seeds.ex: Yerlan described Karaganda for an exchange application. The reviewer wrote: 'the clearest description we received'.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what can visitors do in the mountains near Yerlan's city?
seeds.task: Write about your city or village (35–55 words): where it is, how big it is, two interesting places, what people do there, and what you like about it.
model: Name the city and the country
I live in Almaty, the biggest city in Kazakhstan.
It is in the south, near the mountains.
Almost two million people live here.
There is a green park in the centre and a big market called Zelyony Bazar.
In winter people go to the mountains to ski.
The traffic in the morning is terrible.
I like my city because you can see the mountains from every street.
phr: It is in the … of the country.
There is a … in the centre.
Мне нравится мой город, потому что …
sent: I live in Almaty, the biggest city in Kazakhstan.
It is in the south, near the mountains.
Almost two million people live here.
There is a green park in the centre.
In winter people go to the mountains.
The traffic in the morning is terrible.
Visitors can ski from December to March.
The old market opens at eight.
I do not like the city in July because of the heat.
We moved here five years ago.
topics: There is a green park in the centre and a big market near the station.
The centre of my city has two places every visitor sees.
In winter people ski in the mountains and in summer they walk there.
The mountains work all year.
The traffic in the morning is terrible and the buses are full.
My city has one problem everybody complains about.
ideas: The history of the whole country
My cousin's flat in another city
seeds.title: My city
seeds.sub: Where you live, in five facts

seeds.goal: You can describe a hobby: what it is, when you started, how often you do it, what you need for it and why you like it.
seeds.why: A hobby text gives you the phrases every interview and every new class asks for — and it practises how often and how long.
seeds.ex: Ruslan wrote about chess for a summer school. He was put in the club on the first day.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: how often does Ruslan practise?
seeds.task: Write about your hobby (35–55 words): what it is, when you started, how often you do it, what you need for it, and why you like it.
model: I started to play four years ago with my father.
Say how often you do it
I play twice a week and every Sunday morning.
You do not need much: a board and a clock.
I go to a small club near the library.
Last year I won a school competition.
I like chess because it is quiet and it never repeats.
phr: I go to a club near …
Я хожу в клуб рядом с …
sent: I started to play four years ago.
I play twice a week after school.
You do not need much equipment.
I go to a small club near the library.
Last year I won a school competition.
My father taught me the rules.
A game can take two hours.
I like chess because it is quiet.
We play in the club every Sunday morning.
topics: I play twice a week after school and every Sunday morning at the club.
Chess takes three days of my week.
You need a board, a clock and a person who wants to lose.
The equipment for chess is almost nothing.
Last year I won a school competition and came third in the city.
My results are getting better.
ideas: A sport I do not like
The price of a new phone
seeds.title: My hobby
seeds.sub: What you do, when and why

seeds.goal: You can write a thank-you note: what you say thank you for, one detail about it, and one warm closing line.
seeds.why: A thank-you note is short, formulaic and remembered. In many countries not writing one is noticed immediately.
seeds.ex: Aliya left a thank-you note for her host family in Manchester. They sent a photo of it a year later.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: what does Aliya thank the family for exactly?
seeds.task: Write a thank-you note (25–45 words): who you thank, what for, one detail you remember, one thing you learned, and a warm closing line.
model: Say thank you and what for
Thank you very much for these two weeks in your home.
I will not forget your Sunday breakfast and the walk in the park.
My English got much better because you always spoke slowly with me.
I left a small present from Kazakhstan on the kitchen table.
If you come to Almaty, my family will be very happy.
phr: Мой английский стал лучше, потому что …
I hope to see you again.
sent: Thank you very much for these two weeks.
I will not forget your Sunday breakfast.
My English got much better this month.
You always spoke slowly with me.
I left a small present on the table.
My family will be very happy to meet you.
The room you gave me was very warm.
I can cook your apple pie now.
I hope to see you again next year.
topics: Thank you for the two weeks, the food and the walks in the park.
There are three things I want to thank you for.
You always spoke slowly with me and corrected my mistakes kindly.
You helped my English more than any lesson.
If you come to Almaty, my family will show you the mountains.
Now it is our turn to invite you.
ideas: Who I thank and what for
A complaint about the flight home
seeds.title: A thank-you note
seeds.sub: Three lines that people keep

seeds.goal: You can apologise in writing: say sorry, say what happened, and say what you will do about it.
seeds.why: An apology without a reason and without a next step is just a word. This is the first text where structure changes the result.
seeds.ex: Arman broke a neighbour's window with a ball. His three-line English note ended the problem in one evening.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: what will Arman do to fix the problem?
seeds.task: Write a note of apology (25–45 words): say sorry, say what happened, why it happened, what you will do, and finish politely.
model: I am very sorry about your window.
We were playing football in the yard and my ball hit the glass.
It was an accident and nobody was hurt.
My father will pay for the new glass this week.
We will play in the school stadium from now on.
phr: We will not do it again.
sent: I am very sorry about your window.
We were playing football in the yard.
It was an accident and nobody was hurt.
My father will pay for the new glass.
We will play in the stadium from now on.
I did not want to break anything.
I can help you to clean the floor.
My mother spoke to you yesterday.
topics: We were playing football and the ball hit your window.
Here is exactly what happened yesterday.
My father will pay for the glass this week and I will help.
This is how we will fix it.
We will play in the school stadium from now on.
It will not happen again.
ideas: What I will do about it
The story of my football team
seeds.title: A note of apology
seeds.sub: Sorry, why, and what you will do

seeds.goal: You can explain the way: which bus, where to get off, which streets to take and what to look for.
seeds.why: Directions force you to use imperatives and prepositions of movement correctly — and a mistake here has an immediate cost.
seeds.ex: Zhanna wrote directions for a guest from Germany. He arrived on time and without a single phone call.
seeds.read: Read the directions and find one thing: which building should the guest look for?
seeds.task: Write directions to your home (35–55 words): which transport, where to get off, how far to walk, which turns, and one landmark to look for.
model: Take bus number 12 from the station.
Get off at the fifth stop, near the green pharmacy.
Walk straight for about two hundred metres.
Turn left after the small park.
Look for a yellow building with a blue door.
We live on the third floor, flat 21.
Call me when you get off the bus.
sent: Take bus number 12 from the station.
Get off at the fifth stop.
Walk straight for about two hundred metres.
Turn left after the small park.
Look for a yellow building with a blue door.
We live on the third floor.
The journey takes about twenty minutes.
Call me when you get off the bus.
I met my guest at the airport yesterday.
topics: Take bus 12 and get off at the fifth stop near the pharmacy.
The bus part is simple.
Walk two hundred metres, turn left after the park and look for the yellow building.
The walk takes five minutes.
We are on the third floor, flat 21, and the lift is on the right.
The last part is inside the building.
seeds.title: Directions to my house
seeds.sub: How to get there without a map

seeds.goal: You can write about future plans: where you will go, when, with whom, what you will do and one thing you hope for.
seeds.why: This is where going to and will start to mean different things — and where A1 learners either fix the future or carry the mistake for years.
seeds.ex: Bekzat wrote his summer plans for an English club. His teacher used the text to teach going to for the whole group.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: who is Bekzat going with?
seeds.task: Write about your holiday plans (35–55 words): where you are going, when, with whom, what you are going to do there, and one thing you hope for.
model: This summer I am going to Borovoe.
We are leaving on the tenth of July for ten days.
I am going with my parents and my cousin Sanzhar.
We are going to stay in a small house near the lake.
We are going to swim, walk in the forest and cook outside.
I hope the weather will be warm.
phr: This summer I am going to …
We are going to stay in …
sent: This summer I am going to Borovoe.
We are leaving on the tenth of July.
I am going with my parents and my cousin.
We are going to stay near the lake.
We will swim and walk in the forest.
I hope the weather will be warm.
My father booked the train tickets last week.
I do not want to take my laptop.
We can cook outside in the evening.
The journey takes six hours by train.
topics: We are leaving on the tenth of July and coming back after ten days.
The dates are already fixed.
We are going to swim, walk in the forest and cook outside every evening.
Our days there will be simple.
I am going with my parents and my cousin Sanzhar.
This is a family holiday, not a school trip.
ideas: A holiday I had three years ago
seeds.title: My holiday plans
seeds.sub: Where, when, who with, why

seeds.goal: You can write a short diary entry: what happened today, how you felt and one thing you will do tomorrow.
seeds.why: A diary is the safest place to practise the past simple: nobody corrects you, and the mistakes you repeat become visible.
seeds.ex: Karina wrote four English lines every evening for two months. Her past-tense mistakes fell from six a page to one.
seeds.read: Read the entry and find one thing: why was today a good day for Karina?
seeds.task: Write a diary entry for today (35–55 words): what you did, one good thing, one problem, how you felt, and one plan for tomorrow.
model: I got up late and ran to school without breakfast.
I got a five for my English test.
I lost my bus card somewhere in the school.
Dana helped me to look for it for half an hour.
In the end I was tired but happy.
Tomorrow I am going to get up earlier.
sent: I got up late and ran to school.
I got a five for my English test.
I lost my bus card somewhere in the school.
Dana helped me for half an hour.
In the end I was tired but happy.
Tomorrow I am going to get up earlier.
I did not have time for breakfast.
The teacher gave us a lot of homework.
I can find my card in the lost property room.
It was the longest day of the week.
topics: I got up late, ran to school and forgot my breakfast at home.
The morning started badly.
I got a five for my English test and the teacher read my answer to the class.
One thing went really well today.
I lost my bus card and Dana helped me look for it.
The afternoon had a small disaster in it.
ideas: A film I saw last month
seeds.title: A diary entry
seeds.sub: One day, honestly

seeds.goal: You can write a recipe: the ingredients, the steps in order and one piece of advice.
seeds.why: A recipe is the clearest test of instructions in English: if the reader cannot cook it, the text failed.
seeds.ex: Adil wrote his mother's recipe for an international cooking week. Two families from other countries cooked it correctly.
seeds.read: Read the recipe and find one thing: how long do you cook the eggs?
seeds.task: Write a simple recipe (40–60 words): the name of the dish, four or five ingredients, three or four steps in order, and one piece of advice.
model: This is a very simple breakfast: eggs with tomatoes.
You need ten minutes and one pan.
You need three eggs, two tomatoes, salt and a little oil.
First, cut the tomatoes into small pieces.
Then put them in the hot pan for two minutes.
After that add the eggs and cook everything for three minutes.
Do not add salt at the beginning: the tomatoes lose their water.
sent: You need three eggs and two tomatoes.
First, cut the tomatoes into small pieces.
Then put them in the hot pan.
Do not add salt at the beginning.
My mother cooked it every Saturday.
You can add cheese if you like.
The pan must be hot before you start.
topics: Three eggs, two tomatoes, salt and a little oil. Nothing else.
The list of ingredients is very short.
Cut the tomatoes, fry them for two minutes and add the eggs.
The whole recipe is three steps.
Do not add salt at the beginning and do not use a cold pan.
Two mistakes ruin this dish.
ideas: What my friend eats for breakfast
seeds.title: A simple recipe
seeds.sub: Steps a reader can follow

seeds.goal: You can write a short wish list and explain in one sentence why you want each thing.
seeds.why: Wanting something is easy; explaining why in English is what turns a list into a text.
seeds.ex: Nurai sent a wish list to her aunt abroad. She got the book she wanted, because the reason was in the letter.
seeds.read: Read the list and find one thing: why does Nurai want a dictionary?
seeds.task: Write a wish list for your birthday (30–50 words): three things you want, one sentence about why for each, and one thing you do not need.
model: Here are three things I really want this year.
Name the first thing and why
First, a paper dictionary, because I read English books without the internet.
Name the second thing and why
Second, running shoes, because my old ones are too small.
Name the third thing and why
Third, a ticket to the football match in April.
Say what you do not need
All these things are not expensive.
Thank you, and see you on Saturday!
phr: Here are three things I want.
Вот три вещи, которые я хочу.
sent: Here are three things I really want.
My old running shoes are too small.
I read English books without the internet.
The football match is in April.
My aunt sent me a book last year.
I can use the dictionary at school too.
topics: A paper dictionary, running shoes and a football ticket.
There are three things on my list.
My old shoes are too small and the new ones cost very little.
Two of my wishes are about practical things.
Please, no sweets and no soft toys this year.
There is one thing I do not need.
ideas: A present I got two years ago
seeds.title: A wish list
seeds.sub: What you want and why

seeds.goal: You can write a short formal note: why you missed a lesson, what you did about the work, and one polite request.
seeds.why: This is the first text where you write to somebody with authority. The words change even though the facts stay the same.
seeds.ex: Sultan wrote a note in English after two days of illness. His teacher gave him the extra tasks the same day.
seeds.read: Read the note and find one thing: what does Sultan ask the teacher for?
seeds.task: Write a note to your teacher (30–50 words): say who you are, why you were away, what work you did at home, one polite request, and finish politely.
model: My name is Sultan Zhaksybek from class 9B.
I was ill on Monday and Tuesday and I stayed at home.
Say what you did about the work
I did the exercises from page 42 at home.
Could you tell me what we studied on Tuesday?
I will bring the doctor's note tomorrow.
phr: Я не смог прийти, потому что …
sent: My name is Sultan from class 9B.
I was ill on Monday and Tuesday.
I stayed at home for two days.
I did the exercises from page 42.
Could you tell me what we studied?
I will bring the doctor's note tomorrow.
I do not have the new homework.
My mother called the school on Monday.
I can come after lessons for the extra tasks.
topics: I was ill on Monday and Tuesday and stayed at home with a temperature.
This is why I was not at school.
I did the exercises from page 42 and read the next text.
I did not stop working at home.
Could you tell me what we studied on Tuesday?
There is one thing I need from you.
ideas: Who I am and my class
What work I did at home
What my friend did while I was ill
seeds.title: A note to the teacher
seeds.sub: Why you were away, in four lines

seeds.goal: You can write a short profile for a website or an app: who you are, what you do, what you like and what you are looking for.
seeds.why: A profile is the most-read text you will ever write. It is short, public and it decides whether people answer you.
seeds.ex: Damir wrote an English profile for a language-exchange app. He had three partners in a week.
seeds.read: Read the profile and find one thing: what does Damir want from a language partner?
seeds.task: Write a profile for a language-exchange app (30–50 words): your name and age, where you live, your level, two interests, and what you are looking for.
model: Hi, I am Damir, 16, from Astana.
Say what you speak and learn
I speak Kazakh and Russian, and I am learning English.
My level is elementary, so please write simply.
I am interested in football and in space.
I am usually free after seven in the evening.
I am looking for a partner for short daily messages.
Write to me — I always answer!
phr: I speak … and I am learning …
sent: I am Damir, sixteen, from Astana.
I am learning English at school and online.
I am interested in football and space.
I am usually free after seven.
I am looking for a language partner.
I do not use voice messages.
You can write to me every day.
topics: I speak Kazakh and Russian and I am learning English at school.
Languages are the first thing to say here.
I am interested in football and in space, and I read about both in English.
My interests decide what I want to talk about.
I am free after seven and I answer every message.
Here is how our exchange would work.
ideas: A long story about my school
seeds.title: An online profile
seeds.sub: Twenty words that introduce you

seeds.goal: You can describe clothes: what you wear on different days, what colours you like and one favourite piece with its story.
seeds.why: Clothes vocabulary comes up in shops, at airports and in every description of a person — and it drills plural nouns.
seeds.ex: Zarina described her clothes for a class blog. Her post got the most comments because of one old jacket.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: where did Zarina's favourite jacket come from?
seeds.task: Write about your clothes (30–50 words): what you wear to school, what you wear at the weekend, your favourite colours, and one favourite piece with its story.
model: Say what you wear to school
At school I wear a white shirt and dark trousers.
Say what you wear at the weekend
At the weekend I wear jeans and a big sweater.
Say what you wear in winter
In winter I need a warm coat, a hat and gloves.
I like dark blue and grey more than bright colours.
My favourite thing is an old denim jacket.
Tell its story in one line
It was my mother's jacket when she was a student.
I wear it in every photo because it feels like mine.
sent: At school I wear a white shirt.
At the weekend I wear jeans and a sweater.
In winter I need a warm coat and gloves.
I like dark blue more than bright colours.
My favourite thing is an old denim jacket.
I do not like wearing bright red.
I bought these shoes two years ago.
My sister takes my sweater without asking.
I can wear this jacket in spring and autumn.
topics: A white shirt and dark trousers on school days, jeans and a sweater at the weekend.
My week has two kinds of clothes.
In winter I need a warm coat, a hat and gloves for minus twenty.
Winter changes everything I wear.
It was my mother's jacket when she was a student twenty years ago.
One thing in my wardrobe has a history.
ideas: What I wear at the weekend
One favourite piece and its story
seeds.title: What I wear
seeds.sub: Clothes, weather and one favourite thing

seeds.goal: You can describe a past weekend: what you did on each day, who with, and how it was.
seeds.why: Weekends are the natural home of the past simple. Writing about them every Monday fixes irregular verbs faster than any table.
seeds.ex: Alisher wrote about his weekend every Monday for a term. In the exam he wrote the same text about a new weekend in eight minutes.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what did Alisher do on Sunday evening?
seeds.task: Write about your last weekend (35–55 words): what you did on Saturday, what you did on Sunday, who you were with, one good moment, and how you felt on Monday morning.
model: Say what you did on Saturday
On Saturday morning I helped my father in the garage.
After lunch I met my friends and we played football for two hours.
Say what you did in the evening
In the evening we watched a film at Dana's house.
Say what you did on Sunday
On Sunday we visited my grandmother in the village.
She made beshbarmak and gave us apples from her garden.
Say what you did at the end
On Sunday evening I finished my homework late.
On Monday morning I was tired but the weekend was worth it.
sent: On Saturday morning I helped my father.
After lunch I met my friends in the park.
We played football for two hours.
In the evening we watched a film.
On Sunday we visited my grandmother.
She made beshbarmak for the whole family.
I finished my homework very late.
I did not sleep enough on Sunday.
On Monday morning I was tired.
We can go to the village again next month.
topics: I helped my father in the garage, played football and watched a film.
Saturday had three different parts.
We visited my grandmother and she made beshbarmak for everybody.
Sunday was a family day.
I finished my homework at midnight and got up at seven.
The end of the weekend was hard.
seeds.title: My weekend
seeds.sub: Two days in seven sentences

seeds.goal: You can write a birthday card: a greeting, one warm sentence about the person, a wish and a closing.
seeds.why: Cards are short, but they are the texts people keep. One honest detail is worth ten standard wishes.
seeds.ex: Kamila wrote a card in English for her grandmother's seventieth birthday. It was read out loud at the table.
seeds.read: Read the card and find one thing: what does Kamila thank her grandmother for?
seeds.task: Write a birthday card (25–45 words): a greeting, one warm sentence about the person, one thing you thank them for, a wish for the year, and a closing.
model: Seventy years and you still win at cards.
You are the calmest person in our family.
Thank you for every summer in your house.
Make a wish for the year
I wish you good health and quiet mornings.
I will call you every Sunday this year.
phr: You are the … person in our family.
Ты самый … человек в нашей семье.
sent: Happy birthday to the best grandmother.
Seventy years and you still win at cards.
You are the calmest person in our family.
Thank you for every summer in your house.
I wish you good health and quiet mornings.
I will call you every Sunday.
We made your favourite cake yesterday.
My brother cannot come, but he sends his love.
Your house always smells of bread.
We will visit you in July.
topics: You are the calmest person in our family and you never shout.
This card is about who you are.
Thank you for every summer, every breakfast and every story.
There is a lot to thank you for.
I wish you health, quiet mornings and one more win at cards.
Here are my wishes for this year.
ideas: One honest detail about the person
A list of presents I want
seeds.title: A birthday card
seeds.sub: Three warm lines and a wish

seeds.goal: You can describe your school: where it is, how big it is, what is inside, and what you like and dislike about it.
seeds.why: School is the topic every exchange programme and pen-friend asks about, and it trains there is / there are with numbers.
seeds.ex: Aidos described his school for a partner class in Turkey. They sent back a video of theirs.
seeds.read: Read the text and find one thing: what is the best place in Aidos's school?
seeds.task: Write about your school (35–55 words): where it is, how many students, what is inside the building, one thing you like, and one thing you would change.
model: I study at school number 25 in Almaty.
There are about eight hundred students and forty teachers.
The building has three floors, a big gym and a new computer room.
Outside there is a football pitch and a small garden.
My favourite place is the library on the second floor.
I would change the canteen: it is too small for everybody.
I like my school because the teachers know every student by name.
sent: I study at school number 25 in Almaty.
There are about eight hundred students.
The building has three floors and a big gym.
Outside there is a football pitch.
My favourite place is the library.
The canteen is too small for everybody.
Our teachers know every student by name.
I do not like the long lessons on Thursday.
We painted the classroom last summer.
Students can stay after four for the clubs.
topics: There are eight hundred students, forty teachers and three floors.
My school is bigger than it looks from outside.
The library on the second floor is quiet and it has new English books.
One place in the building is my favourite.
The canteen is too small and there is a queue at every break.
There is one thing I would change tomorrow.
ideas: Where the school is and how big
A teacher I do not like
seeds.title: My school
seeds.sub: The building, the people, the day

connTable.hint: You put one more fact next to the first one.
The second part is a surprise after the first.
You put the events in order.

connItems.why: And puts two facts of the same kind next to each other.
But shows that the second fact is the opposite of the first.
Because gives the reason for the first part.
So shows the result of the first part.
Also adds one more activity to the list.
Then puts the second action after the first in time.
And joins two facts about the same person.
But introduces the problem after the wish.
So links a cause to what happened next.
And joins two things in one list.
But joins a small problem to a positive opinion.
So shows what you do as a result.

tr.why: English always needs the verb to be: I AM from Kazakhstan.
A question with a normal verb starts with do or does.
A negative sentence needs do not or don't before the verb.
With he, she and it the verb takes -s: he works.
Go is irregular: the past form is went.
A singular countable noun needs a or an.
After a number bigger than one the noun takes -s.

ans: I go to school every day.
tr.why: Go takes to before a place: go to school, go to work.

tr.src: In my room a big window.
ans: There is a big window in my room.
tr.why: To say that something exists English uses there is / there are.
Can shows ability, and after it the verb has no to.

ans: Can you give me your phone number, please?
tr.why: An order becomes a request with Can you…, please?
After like the second verb usually takes -ing.

reg.fm: I would like to inform you that I am late.
reg.why: Long official phrases sound strange between friends.
A form takes full, neutral sentences without hey.
With a friend you use short everyday words.

reg.fm: I am sorry, I was ill yesterday.
reg.inf: Hi! I was sick, no lesson for me :)
reg.why: A teacher gets a full sentence and no emoji.

reg.fm: I hereby inform you about my holiday.
reg.why: A postcard is warm and short, not official.

reg.fm: I need a room for two nights.
reg.why: Gimme is spoken slang and never goes in writing.
A friend answers a simple question faster than an official one.
Three exclamation marks look like shouting.

reg.fm: I would like to invite you.
reg.why: An invitation to a friend is a direct, happy sentence.

reg.fm: Sorry, I was not at home.
reg.why: Even a short note keeps capital letters and full words.

reg.ctx: A form for a language course
reg.inf: My English is so bad haha
reg.why: A form asks for facts, not jokes about yourself.

reg.ctx: A birthday card for your grandmother
reg.fm: I wish you good health and happiness.
reg.why: For older family members English keeps full words.

opts: Strong and short: one word instead of two.
This means 'so-so' — weaker than the original.
Sounds like you did not really like it.
imp.why: Very + adjective is the weakest way to praise something.

opts: This says nothing about the size.
Nice is about your feeling, not about the size.
imp.why: English has one word for many 'very + adjective' pairs.

opts: Two facts the reader can picture.
Still no information about the weather.
Strange does not tell the reader what to wear.
imp.why: Facts beat opinions when you describe the weather.

opts: Sleepy means you want to sleep, not that you worked hard.
imp.why: Choose the word that already has 'very' inside it.

imp.sent: My friend is a good person.
opts: Two real qualities instead of one empty word.
Fine is what you say about the weather.
Normal sounds cold about a friend.
imp.why: Good is the emptiest adjective in English.

opts: The exact word for very tasty food.
This means you can eat it — nothing more.
imp.why: Food words are precise in English: delicious, salty, spicy.

imp.sent: I said a small word about my hobby.
imp.why: In writing, say exactly what and how much you wrote.

opts: One word for a city with a long history.
A negative that gives no picture.
imp.why: Precise adjectives make a short text sound grown-up.

imp.sent: I have a lot of things to do.
opts: A number is the clearest possible detail.
Work is uncountable: 'many works' is a mistake.
imp.why: Numbers are the cheapest way to sound precise.

opts: Natural English: fun takes great, not very.
Funny means it made you laugh.
imp.why: Fun and funny are different words: fun = enjoyable, funny = making you laugh.

imp.sent: I want to say thank you very much.
opts: Just say it — no announcement needed.
Fine, but too formal for a friend.
imp.why: Do not announce what you are going to say. Say it.

imp.sent: My house is near from the school.
opts: Near needs no preposition: near the school.
Nearly means almost — a different word.
imp.why: Near takes no preposition; close takes to.

tl.long: I am writing this message to you today because I want to say that I am late.
tl.why: The announcement 'I am writing to say' eats half the message.

tl.long: My name is Aidana and my age is fifteen years old and I live in the city of Almaty.
tl.model: I am Aidana, I am fifteen and I live in Almaty.
tl.why: 'My age is … years old' says the same thing twice.

tl.long: The weather here in this place is very very hot and also very sunny every day.
tl.model: The weather here is hot and sunny.
tl.why: Double 'very' and 'here in this place' add nothing.

tl.long: I would like to say that I like playing football with my friends very much.
tl.model: I love playing football with my friends.
tl.why: 'I would like to say that' is an empty opening.

tl.long: There is a big window in my room and the window is very big and new.
tl.model: My room has a big new window.
tl.why: The same window is described twice.

tl.long: I want to invite you to come to my birthday party on Saturday at six o'clock.
tl.model: Come to my birthday party on Saturday at six.
tl.why: 'I want to invite you to come' is three verbs for one action.

tl.long: The thing that I like most of all about my city is that it is very green.
tl.model: I like my city because it is green.
tl.why: 'The thing that I like most of all is that' can always be cut.

tl.long: I am sending you this postcard so that you can know that I am fine here.
tl.model: I am fine here in Turkey.
tl.why: The reader already knows it is a postcard.

tl.long: My mother she works in a hospital in the centre of the city as a doctor.
tl.model: My mother is a doctor in the city hospital.
tl.why: 'My mother she' repeats the subject twice.

tl.long: I go to the shop and buy some bread and after that I go back to my home.
tl.model: I buy bread and go home.
tl.why: Everyday actions do not need every step written down.

distract: My grandmother has a cat called Mia.
The paragraph is not about pets: one private detail breaks the topic.
Yesterday I watched a film about space.
A different day and a different subject — it does not belong here.
I do not like tomatoes at all.
Food opinions have nothing to do with this paragraph.
My brother plays computer games every evening.
The paragraph is about you, not about your brother's evenings.
The bus number 12 goes to the station.
A transport detail that the reader does not need here.
I have three pencils in my bag.
A random object: it adds no information to the topic.
My favourite colour is green.
Colours are a different subject.
The shop closes at eight in the evening.
Opening hours belong to another text.
I want to buy new shoes next month.
Future shopping plans are off the topic here.
My cousin lives in another city.
Family geography does not develop this paragraph.
It was very cold last winter.
Last winter is a different time and a different story.
I like listening to music on the bus.
A habit that does not belong to this paragraph.

topics.body: It has two rooms, a small kitchen and a balcony. The windows look at the park.
topics.right: I want to tell you about my flat.

topics.body: I get up at seven, have breakfast and go to school at eight. I come home at three.
topics.right: This is my normal school day.

topics.body: She is tall and she has long dark hair. She always helps me with maths.
topics.right: My best friend is called Dana.

topics.body: We swim in the sea every morning and eat ice cream in the evening.
topics.right: We are on holiday in Turkey.

topics.body: First you take two eggs. Then you put them in hot water for five minutes.
topics.right: This is how I make my breakfast.

topics.body: It starts at six on Saturday. There will be music, a cake and ten friends.
topics.right: I am having a birthday party.

topics.body: I feed him in the morning and take him for a walk after school.
topics.right: I have a dog called Bars.

topics.body: On Monday I have maths, English and history. Tuesday is my long day.
topics.right: This is my timetable at school.

tsWrong: My father drives a blue car.
We have a big table in the kitchen.
The weather was terrible in winter.
offIdeas: What I ate for breakfast today
The reader learns nothing about your topic from your breakfast.
My opinion about a film I saw
A different subject: it belongs in a review, not here.
Prices of your things are not part of this text.
A story about my neighbour's dog
Someone else's pet takes the reader away from your point.
Future plans belong to another text.
The name of my first teacher
A private detail with no job in this text.
Your mood right now does not help the reader.
Off topic: keep one subject per text.

outlineRules.msg: The greeting and the reason always come first: the reader must know at once what the text is.
New facts cannot stand in the closing — the last lines only finish the text.

rubric.task: Did you answer every part of the task? At A1 that means: all the facts the task asks for.
rubric.organisation: Are the sentences in a logical order, with and, but, because between them?
rubric.vocabulary: Did you use the topic words, or only 'good', 'bad' and 'nice'?
rubric.grammar: Word order, the verb to be, articles a/an and -s with he, she, it.
